residence_time_min.text: Calculation (Step 2) estimated τ = 0.3 min for a 1 mm ID open tube, but this assumed a much smaller reactor. The available reactor is the 0.3 mL CatCart (inventory: reactor_cuc_cart_030). Using V/Q = 0.3 mL / 0.1 mL/min = 3.0 min, which exactly matches the batch microwave reaction time (3 min). Analogy 1 (similar [3+2] cycloaddition, 60°C, 20 min) and Analogy 2 (thermal, 195°C, 4 min) both support multi-minute residence times for thermally driven cycloadditions; our 3 min at 150°C is consistent. Analogy 1 difference: lower temperature (60°C vs 150°C) and different substrate class — longer τ needed at lower T; our higher T justifies shorter τ. Analogy 2 difference: Claisen rearrangement, not CuAAC — used as confirmation that 4 min at high T is feasible, not for direct parameter transfer.
residence_time_min.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

residence_time_basis.text: Single-phase liquid system (no gas reagents). Basis = reactor_volume / liquid_flow_rate = 0.3 mL / 0.1 mL/min = 3.0 min. inlet/STP basis not applicable (no gas feed).

temperature_C.text: Directly from batch protocol (150°C) and Chemistry Plan stage 1. Analogies 1 and 2 confirm elevated temperature operation is feasible in flow. No reason to deviate from batch-proven temperature for first flow experiment.

BPR_bar.text: Calculation Step 8: P_vap(acetone, 150°C) = 11.3 bar; BPR required. Only available BPR setpoint is 20.0 bar (bpr_xcube_20). 20 bar > 11.3 bar — adequate margin (~8.7 bar). Chemistry Plan incompatible_pairs explicitly flags acetone at 150°C without back-pressure. Analogy 2 also used BPR for high-temperature operation.
BPR_bar.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

flow_rate_mL_min.text: Set to 0.1 mL/min (minimum of pump_xcube_hplc range: 0.1–3.0 mL/min) to achieve 3.0 min residence time in the 0.3 mL CatCart. Q = V/τ = 0.3/3.0 = 0.1 mL/min. This is the minimum pump flow, which is appropriate for a first screening experiment. Analogy 1 used 0.165 mL/min — similar order of magnitude, supporting feasibility.

chemistry_notes.text: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene on heterogeneous Cu/C packed-bed CatCart. Key design decisions: (1) Single-stream feed is safe because no Cu catalyst is present in solution at room temperature — premixing benzyl azide and phenylacetylene in acetone does not initiate reaction. (2) 150 °C operation requires 20 bar BPR to keep acetone (bp 56 °C, P_vap ~11.3 bar at 150 °C) in liquid phase — the only available BPR setpoint (20 bar) is adequate. (3) Residence time of 3.0 min matches the batch microwave time exactly, using the full 0.3 mL CatCart volume at 0.1 mL/min (minimum pump flow). (4) The CatCart provides ~0.3 mmol Cu per cartridge; at 0.025 mmol/min limiting substrate throughput (0.25 M × 0.1 mL/min), effective Cu loading per pass is ~12 mol%, consistent with the 10 mol% batch loading. (5) Energetic azide safety: flow confines benzyl azide inventory at 150 °C to <0.3 mL at any instant — a major safety advantage over batch microwave. Blast shield (safety_cuaac_shield) mandatory throughout. (6) Analogies retrieved had low similarity scores (0.053–0.069) and different reaction classes; hardware parameters were derived primarily from the batch protocol and engineering calculations. (7) Axial dispersion warning from calculations (Pe ~4 for 1 mm ID tubing) is not applicable here — the packed-bed CatCart (4 mm ID, 0.3 mL) operates in a different flow regime; packed beds inherently reduce axial dispersion relative to open tubes. (8) No deoxygenation required per Chemistry Plan.
chemistry_notes.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

controls.description: Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Leak- and pressure-test the assembled system before reagent introduction.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Minimize azide feed inventory and reactive holdup.
Stop feeds and cool before responding to blockage; never open under pressure.
Prevent unassessed metal-azide accumulation and stagnant zones.
Operate behind declared shielding or enclosed containment.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 10 mL final-volume basis, charge benzyl azide: 2.5 mmol (0.25 M final); phenylacetylene: 2.75 mmol (0.275 M final); add acetone to 10 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 20 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.

Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 7.2 min, based on three nominal liquid-volume turnovers. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present.

operating_procedure.instruction: After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 2.4 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.

validation_experiments.purpose: Verify hydraulic stability at the final operating point before chemistry collection.
validation_experiments.procedure: Run compatible blank solvent at Q=0.125 mL/min, T=150.0 C, and BPR=20 bar for at least 10 min; record flow, temperature, pressure, leaks, and blockage indicators.

validation_experiments.purpose: Measure the residence-time distribution and phase holdup at the operating point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Introduce a compatible nonreactive tracer at Q=0.125 mL/min and measure its outlet response after correcting for external tubing delay. Report the measured mean, dispersion and liquid holdup separately from the calculated 2.4 min index (liquid-only reactor volume / liquid flow); do not require agreement with an STP turnover index.

validation_experiments.purpose: Generate the first wet-lab response at the exact canonical design point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Execute the canonical operating procedure once and report conversion, isolated yield, selectivity, pressure trace, temperature trace, and any phase or blockage observations.

intensification.basis: Predicted screening target: 6.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: kinetic. Primary flow advantage: hazardous_intermediate. Mechanisms: hazardous-intermediate holdup reduction, selectivity-sensitive stream logic.
